_comment: The entered-once index of the base catalog shipped with the plugin. Every file under catalog/ (bar this one) is listed here exactly once, with the real need it answers. turma:bootstrap selects from this list; scripts/check.mjs proves the list and the directory agree. A user's own additions live in an overlay catalog under TURMA_HOME, never here. catalogVersion tracks plugin.json version - any change here is a plugin change.

blocks.grounds: Every commit, by a person or by Claude, must be visible to turma:optimize. git's post-commit hook is the only trigger that catches both; a Claude Code hook only sees commits Claude makes.
The optimizer runs on demand, so a backlog is easy to forget. At session end, if commits sit unreviewed past optimizer-state.json, a notification names the count.
After Claude commits, a one-line reminder that the queue grew and turma:optimize is the thing to run keeps the loop visible without running analysis mid-flow.

In accept-edits / auto mode Claude reads files outside the repo with no prompt. This blocks an outside-repo Read/Grep/Glob (allow list: the repo, the Turma source, ~/.claude, scratch dirs, TURMA_READ_ALLOW). Same reasoning as no-build-over-dev-server: a warn-only hook is ignored in the mode that needs it.

next build writes over .next while next dev serves from it; every route then 500s with 'Cannot find module' until the server restarts and .next is cleared. The message names nothing. Ports come from TURMA_DEV_PORTS or .claude/launch.json.

The shape of the drift-auditor example (examples/agents/drift-auditor.md): read a diff, run the repo's own checker, defer to its verdict, report without fixing. Fill in the repo's source-of-truth and generated files.
The shape of the schema-warden example (examples/agents/schema-warden.md): a data-shape change is half a change; write the migration, update every companion file, run the checker until green.
The shape of the render-verifier example (examples/agents/render-verifier.md): render the real artifact, assert against extracted text and measured pages, never against the code that produced them.
A repo with a guard script wants that script run, and its output read, before a PR opens. The skill wraps the exact command and refuses to pass on a silent skip.
A repo that generates files from a source (README from data, screenshots from the app) wants one command that regenerates all of them and shows the diff.
Confirming a change in the real app, not just the tests: launch on the repo's port (launch.json), drive it, capture a screenshot.
The rule Turma is built to defend, stated once so each CLAUDE.md carries the same words.
A description rule worth reusing wherever prose ships to a reader: one sentence, no marketing words, do not start with the subject's own name.
A repo-wide typographic rule is cheap to state and annoying to retrofit; this states one (no em dashes).
A CLAUDE.md is more useful with a map of the tree and the common tasks; this is the skeleton for that section.
A secret in .env or .env.local should never land in context. Every repo with local secrets wants this deny list.
The settings.json fragment that wires the Claude Code hooks: the SessionEnd nudge, the after-commit context nudge, and the read-outside-repo guard. Merged into a repo's settings by the bootstrap.
turma:define needs one shape for a problem doc so docs/problems/<slug>.md means the same thing in every repo instead of each one inventing its own.
turma:design writes docs/decisions/NNNN-title.md ADRs, each with Status/Context/Decision/Consequences, the common ADR layout, so every repo's decisions read the same way.
turma:design fills one skeleton for a topic doc (orientation, source of truth, generated, guard, decisions) instead of free-form prose a checker cannot recognise.
A ticket that does not cite the design section it implements is invented, not grounded - the house rule extended to GitHub Issues. turma:tickets fills this for every issue it opens.
Every repo can run problem -> design -> tickets -> work; a CLAUDE.md that never mentions the loop leaves it undiscoverable to a fresh Claude Code session.
turma:init needs one shape for a new repo README so turma:bootstrap and turma:design read the same section names (what it produces, source of truth, generated, stack, guard) in every project.
